latin: Vna est anima intellectiua in omnibus hominibus.
translation: There is one intellective soul in all human beings.
translation_note: 'anima intellectiua' is the intellective soul; the thesis states in bare form the doctrine of the unity of the intellect associated with Averroes (farmer1998:12937).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch8, from Latin at farmer1998:12937

sources.text: the problem of the unity of the intellect, discussed together under theses 7.2-7.4
sources.pico_relation: Farmer's note groups this thesis with 7.3-7.4 as concerning the unity of the intellect and cross-references Pico's own theses 3>67-69

doctrine: The thesis asserts flatly that there is one intellective soul in all human beings (farmer1998:12937). Farmer's note groups it together with the two theses that follow, 7.3 and 7.4, under the problem of the unity of the intellect, and directs the reader to Pico's own theses 3>67-69 (farmer1998:12967). A footnote in the Dougherty anthology quotes the Latin of this thesis verbatim and likewise cross-references Conclusions 3>67-9 (dougherty2008:9366).
context: Farmer's cross-reference network for this run of theses also includes 18.1, attributed to Alexander of Aphrodisias, which asserts that the rational soul is immortal (farmer1998:14716), and 20.7, attributed to Plotinus, on the soul's final happiness in union with the first intellect (farmer1998:15105); both bear on the same question of the individuality and fate of the intellect that this thesis raises in Averroes' name.
historiography: The only scholarship on this thesis found in the material opened is the brief citation in the Dougherty anthology, which quotes the Latin and cross-references 3>67-9 without further comment (dougherty2008:9366).
not_established: Any scholarly discussion of this thesis beyond the bare citation in the Dougherty footnote is not established by the sources consulted.
Whether Pico intends the thesis to state Averroes' own doctrine of a single shared intellect precisely, as opposed to a scholastic simplification of it, is not addressed in the material consulted.
